findings.claim: Requirement says all generated code must be decorated, but the attribute is suppressed under #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK. Consumers targeting netstandard2.0 or .NET Framework still get undecorated generated code, so coverage skew remains there. The README documents this limit, but the requirement does not record it as acceptable. The guard also misses other TFMs where the attribute is absent (e.g. older netcoreapp, netstandard2.1 is fine).

receipt_plan.detail: Compile generated output with a netstandard2.0 target and count ExcludeFromCodeCoverage occurrences. The attribute is inside an inactive #if block, so the types are undecorated. Compare with the requirement 'all generated code'.

findings.claim: The nested-type namespace emitter change ("{" to "{\r\n") alters output for every nesting type with constraints. It is unrelated to the attribute requirement and changes snapshot formatting beyond the attribute, which is a scope expansion in the generator that L4 notes is fix-prone.

receipt_plan.detail: Rerun snapshot tests and inspect diffs for nested generic-constrained types. Confirm that the only changes are the attribute lines and this newline.

findings.claim: The generator emits a preprocessor symbol check (NETSTANDARD2_0/NETFRAMEWORK) evaluated in the consumer's compilation. The test only checks text, never that the output compiles on a netstandard2.0 or net framework consumer, and no test compiles generated code with the attribute active.

receipt_plan.detail: Mutate the guard to `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` or remove the attribute fully qualified `global::` prefix. The string-matching tests would catch some but not compile failures. Add a compile test per TFM.

questions.text: Should the attribute be emitted unconditionally for all targets, with a polyfill or fallback on netstandard2.0/.NET Framework, or is skipping those targets acceptable?
options: Emit on all targets by also defining the attribute or using a different approach
questions.why_it_matters: If skipping is acceptable, the change meets the requirement. If every target must be covered, the guard is a requirement miss.

interpretations.label: A
interpretations.summary: Unconditional with no setting: every generated type (formatters, resolvers, nested helper classes) gets [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage] guarded by #if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK, and no opt-out option exists.

interpretations.label: B
interpretations.summary: Same decoration but with an opt-out MSBuild or generator option (e.g. a MessagePackGeneratorOptions flag) so that users who want coverage of generated code can disable the attribute. Templates would take an option flag and emit the attribute only when enabled.
